literal: Evils having diminished, virtue will increase, good things having sought, pleasant words if one speaks.
translation: If one seeks to do good and speaks pleasant words, their sins will diminish and virtue will grow.
modern: நன்மையானவற்றை விரும்பி, இனிமையான சொற்களைப் பேசினால், பாவங்கள் தேய்ந்து அழியும்; அறம் பெருகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the transformative power of kind speech. When a person actively seeks out what is good (நல்லவை நாடி) and speaks sweet, pleasant words (இனிய சொலின்), it brings about a dual effect. Their vices and past sins (அல்லவை) gradually wear away and diminish (தேய), while their righteousness and moral virtue (அறம்) grow and flourish (பெருகும்). The poet shows that pleasant speech is not just a social courtesy but a powerful practice that purifies one's character.
